source.title: Automated learning rate search using batch-level cross-validation

record.tranche_reason: Tests a new batch-level learning-rate search method on image-classification datasets and reports held-out test accuracy against macro-CV SGD-with-momentum baselines. It does not test the specific claim versions listed.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the study's own test-accuracy comparisons for its micro-CV training method and macro-CV baseline. Cited results about Adam, SGD, cyclical learning rates, and deep bilevel learning are not rows. Epoch counts, losses, computational costs, and wall-clock times are omitted because they are not separate measures of the held-out generalization behavior at issue.
record.test_reason: The study uses prior findings about SGD versus adaptive optimizers to motivate its choice of momentum SGD, then evaluates its own learning-rate selection method. Both comparison arms use momentum SGD; none of V1–V8 is tested. Calling the learning-rate schedule adaptive does not make this an Adam-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: selected micro-CV configurations achieve competitive accuracy with lower total cross-validation cost, including 81.03% versus 81.50% on CIFAR-10 and 52.50% versus 51.02% on Adience. Qualify this as applying to selected configurations: several lambda settings perform substantially worse, and some take longer than macro-CV. The authors explicitly leave comparison with Adam, AdaGrad, and RMSprop to future research.
record.recipe_differences: Micro-CV selects a learning rate per epoch using losses on randomly split half-batches; the baseline uses dataset-level macro-CV and early stopping to select SGD-with-momentum learning-rate schedules. Both use SGD with momentum.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracy varies with lambda, dataset, and architecture; the best relative result differs across those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: All reported micro-CV accuracies are below their macro-CV baselines on CIFAR-10 and SVHN. On Adience, lambda 0.5 reaches 52.50% versus 51.02%, while the other lambda settings perform worse. Accuracy and computational savings depend strongly on configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-level cross-validation can select momentum-SGD learning-rate schedules with competitive held-out accuracy and reduced total tuning cost in some configurations.

record.peer_reviewed: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences, Vol. 4, No. 3, December 2021
record.problems: The reported accuracies are averages over repeated runs, but no error bars or variability estimates are given. The experiments compare learning-rate selection procedures while holding the optimizer to SGD with momentum; they do not test random-label memorization or the other listed mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported test-accuracy comparisons were left out. Other table measures (epochs, test loss, theoretical cost, and time cost) were not extracted as separate rows because they do not independently measure the held-out generalization outcome cataloged here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, matched natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching; these are discussed through prior work only.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and mitigation of large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The table accuracies match the extracted values. All rows belong under fits_no_version rather than as evidence for V1–V8. The paper's accuracy/time summaries sometimes combine different configurations: CIFAR-10 small-CNN accuracy 73.59% takes 19min 38s in Table 2, not 8min 37s; VGG-11 accuracy 73.91% takes 24min 9s. No uncertainty estimates establish statistical significance for the Adience improvement.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the effects of local connectivity.
Comparison of adaptive optimizers such as Adam with SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning; effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and mitigation by changing the training recipe.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized examples and retraining.
